title: Codes and pulse with gaps
prompt: A data-quality report counts each visit's diagnosis codes next to its pulse. Some feeds send an empty list of codes, or no list at all. Write `solve(encounters)` so it returns `encounter_id`, `code_count` and `heart_rate`.
rules: `code_count` is the number of items in `diagnosis_codes`. An empty list counts 0; a visit with no list at all has a missing count.
`heart_rate` is the field inside `vitals`. It is missing when the visit has no vitals, or when the pulse wasn't taken.
Return the three columns, in that order, for every visit, duplicates included.
hints: `F.size("diagnosis_codes")` counts the items of an array.
An empty list and a missing list are different things: one has no items, the other isn't there. Check what `F.size` gives for each.
Don't pick items out of the list: an empty list has no position 0, and asking for it stops the job.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(encounters):
    # encounter_id, code_count, heart_rate
    return encounters
explanation: `encounters.select("encounter_id", F.size("diagnosis_codes").alias("code_count"), "vitals.heart_rate")`. `F.size` already treats the two gaps differently: an empty list has 0 items, and a missing list gives a missing count (with Spark 4's default settings). Reading `heart_rate` from a missing `vitals` gives a missing value, the same as a struct whose `heart_rate` is itself missing. Anything that picks `diagnosis_codes[0]` fails on an empty list, because Spark 4 stops when a position doesn't exist. Counting the last position (`size - 1`) is off by one.
